title: Refactor executor/reactor to isolate KV cache compaction from scheduler event loop
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Reduce p99 tail latency spikes caused by synchronous KV cache compaction work running on the scheduler's reactor. This ticket refactors the executor/reactor separation, extracts the compaction path into an independent compactor worker with cooperative backpressure, and prepares a safe canary rollout. We will also upgrade the async runtime dependency to tokio 1.20 and bump the protobuf/prost toolchain to address a GC-related allocation pattern. Deliverables: (1) non-blocking compactor worker, (2) executor/reactor API split with clear handoff points, (3) dependency upgrades with migration notes, (4) benchmarks and monitoring dashboards documenting regressions/improvements.
acceptance_criteria: p99 tail latency for short-gen workload reduced by >= 10% in controlled benchmark relative to baseline (same model, same batch sizes)
No scheduler reactor stalls > 50ms observed in production canary for 48 hours
KV compaction runs moved off reactor thread and report compaction metrics (duration, queue depth, last run) to console
All unit and integration tests pass; new end-to-end test reproduces compaction backpressure scenario
Rollout plan executed with canary -> regional -> global progression and automatic rollback on SLO regressions
plan: Spike: prototype compactor worker in a sidecar threadpool (branch: feat/compactor-spike) — 3d
Define executor/reactor boundary interfaces and add feature-flagged handoff points — 4d
Implement compactor queue with backpressure tokens and non-blocking metrics hooks — 5d
Upgrade tokio to 1.20 and prost to 0.12 in a separate PR; run test matrix and fix API changes — 2d
Integrate compactor into mainline behind feature flag; add integration tests and benchmarks — 4d
Canary rollout to one Dedicated pool with telemetry dashboards and alerting thresholds — 2d
Full rollout, monitoring sweep, and postmortem after 72h — 1d
risks: Dependency upgrade may introduce runtime behavior changes causing rare deadlocks; mitigate by keeping tokio upgrade in isolated PR and running stress tests
Compaction worker could change memory pressure profile leading to OOMs if not bounded; mitigate with hard queue limits and memory-aware admission
Feature-flag complexity may cause divergence between canary and prod; schedule a short-lived tech cleanup to remove flags after rollout
Instrumentation gaps: if compaction metrics are incomplete, rollback criteria may be unclear; add explicit gauges before canary
